slides.headline: RealPage rent-pricing cases draw Miami renters
slides.body: Lawsuits accuse RealPage of antitrust violations and price fixing tied to rent-pricing software.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Miami apartment building high rise rental
photo.prompt: Close street-level view of a Miami high-rise apartment building with stacked balconies and a leasing sign, no people

slides.headline: That case centers on rent-pricing software
slides.body: RealPage produces property management software for algorithmic rent setting and is headquartered in Texas.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons apartment leasing office computer
photo.prompt: Leasing office desk with a laptop showing a generic rent chart, apartment keys and paperwork in sharp focus, no people

slides.headline: And DOJ sued RealPage in 2024
slides.body: The United States Department of Justice sued RealPage in 2024, alleging its software represented a price-fixing scheme to raise rents.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons United States Department of Justice building
photo.prompt: Exterior of the United States Department of Justice building with columns and the DOJ seal visible, no people

slides.headline: Which puts 24M housing units in the background
slides.body: RealPage services are used on more than 24 million housing units worldwide across several rental markets.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons apartment towers aerial Miami
photo.prompt: Aerial view of dense apartment towers and condo buildings in Miami with streets below, late afternoon, no people

slides.headline: The reason: alleged coordinated rent hikes
slides.body: Lawsuits claim RealPage software helped landlords coordinate pricing and pressured customers to follow rent suggestions.

slides.headline: So Miami renters are watching the cases
slides.body: The next issue is how courts and settlements define any renter claims tied to RealPage pricing tools.
